subject: general
question: In the context of inflation, what does CPI mean?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumer Price Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• CPI stands for **Consumer Price Index**. Here are some details about the CPI:
 
• **The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures** the average change over time in the prices paid by consumers for a representative basket of goods and services.
 
• **The CPI tracks price changes for a variety of consumer essentials, including**:
 
 
• Food
 
• Housing
 
• Transportation
 
• Medical care
 
• Other daily living expenses
 
 
 
• **Price data is collected at regular intervals**.
 
• Weighting diagrams represent consumption patterns, assigning weights to products based on their share of household spending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governments and central banks utilize** the CPI to** target inflation and monitor price stability.**
 
• The CPI helps in **indexing dearness allowances for employees and adjusting tax brackets.**
 
• Businesses and individuals use the CPI to **adjust wages and rents.**
